title: kv-cache-reuse-eviction-scratchpad
content:
Purpose / context:
Quick experimental notes and observability outputs while investigating unusual token-level latency spikes on p3d.xlarge nodes. Focused on KV (key-value) cache management: reuse rates, eviction behavior under mixed chat workloads, paging signs, and memory bandwidth effects. Goal is to produce reproducible microbenchmarks and a prioritized remediation list for Q2 runtime work.

High-level hypothesis:
- High tail latency correlates with low KV reuse on chat workloads with heavy multi-session interleaving; eviction churn increases DRAM reads and kernel-level memcpy pressure leading to bandwidth saturation on some NVMe-backed swap paths.
- Not a model compute problem (kernels look healthy) but rather cache thrash + memory subsystem effects when KV store grows >~70% of available GPU host pinned memory and fallback to host memory happens.

Experiment matrix (quick):
1) Baseline: steady single-session generation (seq_len 1024, batch=1, model shard local) -> expected reuse ~98%
2) Multi-session random prefix: 128 concurrent sessions, average prompt length 80, tail token generation 512 -> measure reuse, evictions/sec
3) Mixed short/long sessions: 64 short (avg 32 tokens) + 32 long (avg 1024 tokens)
4) Stress-add background prefetch threads, simulate client reconnects causing KV invalidations

Metrics collected (how):
- KV reuse rate: hits / (hits+misses) sampled per-epoch (window=1m).
- Evictions/sec: counted from allocator hooks (LRU list pops).
- Memory bandwidth: via /sys/devices/system/node and nvlink stats (where available) and perf counters (mem_uops for host; nvidia-smi dmon for GPU).
- Page faults and swap activity: /proc/vmstat & sar -B, plus dmesg pattern for OOM-killer; on nodes with host memory pressure used pmap dumps.
- Latency percentiles: p50/p95/p99 token generation measured at the request edge.

Representative run notes (2026-02-24):
- Node type: p3d.8xlarge equivalent (96GB host, 8xA100 40GB), but only using 1 GPU for this test with shared host memory.
- Config: KV store size limit set to 48GB host-side; eviction policy: LRU single-queue; continuous batching enabled (max batch 16).
- Workload: scenario 2 (128 sessions). Duration: 40m

Observations:
- KV reuse dropped to 57% median across windowed samples (range 51% - 66%).
- Evictions peaked at 12k/sec during concurrent long tail bursts; steady-state ~1.2k/sec.
- Host memory bandwidth (measured via perf) showed periodic spikes aligning with eviction bursts: observed sustained 6.8 GB/s reads for ~20s windows (baseline idle ~1.1 GB/s).
- p99 token latency correlated strongly with eviction spikes: p99 rose from 210ms -> 920ms during peak.
- Swap/page activity: occasional minor soft page faults increased by ~18x during peaks; no full swap-to-disk observed, but kernel reported increased anonymous page reclaim activity.
- Kernel logs: several messages similar to "mmc_read_ahead" and DMA remapping churn; no OOM.

Quick flamegraph/CPU profile notes (sample during eviction spike):
- Top consumer threads: kv_evict_worker, kv_reclaim_loop, memcpy_from_host (bulk), request_scheduler (blocked on wait for kv).
- Hot functions: copy_to_gdr_copy(), host_page_walk(), slab_free_objects().
- Suggests heavy host->device copy work and allocator churn.

Policy experiments (A/B):
A) LRU (baseline): lower reuse, higher eviction/sec, higher p99.
B) Segmented LRU (hot/cold buckets, promote on repeat accesses): reuse improved to ~73% with same memory cap; evictions/sec down by ~45%; p99 decreased to ~330ms.
C) FIFO (experiment): poor — reuse ~48%, worse misses for repeated prefixes.
D) TTL-based time-window: TTL=120s reduced evictions for very active sessions but increased memory pressure causing more host paging for medium activity.

Memory placement experiments:
- Host-pinned vs host-swappable region: pinning KV buffers (mlock) reduced page fault spikes and improved p99 by ~15% at cost of higher host RAM reservation.
- On nodes with HBM-backed NVMe (testbed): observed lower memcopy time; on non-local bursty eviction we saw 30% lower p99 when using pinned host buffer + cudaMemcpyAsync pinned path.

Microbenchmark: single-key reuse test
- Setup: repeatedly access the same KV entry at increasing inter-arrival intervals (1ms...1000ms)
- Result: reuse probability drops sharply after 200ms inter-arrival when background eviction pressure >500 evictions/sec; indicates typical working-set churn window ~150-250ms for our workload mix.

Insights / probable root causes:
1) Eviction churn under mixed concurrent short/long sessions reduces reuse rates causing frequent large memcpy operations from host->GPU which saturate host memory bandwidth and increase token latency at tail.
2) Current single-queue LRU is too aggressive for mixed hot/cold access patterns (does not retain recently-reused embeddings long enough).
3) Host memory fragmentation and lack of pinned allocations increases page faults under eviction bursts, exacerbating latency spikes.
4) Continuous batching helps throughput but can worsen worst-case latency when a batch has many cache misses that trigger memcopies.

Immediate mitigations (cheap / low-risk):
- Switch default policy to segmented LRU (hot/cold) with small hot-size (10% of limit) to keep frequently re-referenced KVs around.
- Increase default KV pin threshold for sessions with high-reuse signals (detect repeated prefixes and pin their keys for short TTL).
- Add soft backpressure: if eviction/sec > threshold, reduce max batch size to cut down concurrent memcopy amplification.

Design & implementation tasks (next cycle):
- Implement a lightweight per-key recency counter to enable 2Q/SLRU semantics. (PR prototype exists: github:repo/serving-runtime#789 — review req'd)
- Add alloc tracer that samples host allocation sizes and fragmentation to guide pinning policy.
- Instrument memory bandwidth SLIs per node; surface these in the console per-deployment.
- Evaluate use of hugepages / mlock-all for dedicated nodes vs tradeoffs for multi-tenant boxes.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Interaction with model quantization memory layouts: does smaller KV per-entry (int8 distillations) change eviction pressure linearly or cause different fragmentation? Need targeted experiment.
- Are some customer request patterns causing pathological reuse loss (bot farms re-opening many ephemeral sessions)? Suggest customer sampling for heavy-eviction tenants.
- How does fallback to non-pinned host memory affect CUDA transfer pipeline in our runtime (async overlap expectations may be violated)? Need deeper kernel-level tracing.

Quick action list (owner / ETA):
- [Aisha] flip to SLRU in staging for 48hr soak -> measure reuse/latency (ETA: 2026-03-08).
- [Ben] add eviction/sec + mem-bandwidth SLI dashboard tile (ETA: 2026-03-05).
- [Rosa] run per-customer trace for top-5 tenants during peak window to detect pathological access patterns (ETA: 2026-03-12).
- [Ethan] prototype pinned-allocation option for dedicated pools and run swap-free test (ETA: 2026-03-20).

Notes / scratch ideas:
- Consider low-overhead directory of hot keys (bloom filter-ish) maintained per-GPU rather than global to avoid lock contention on LRU lists.
- Explore adaptive batch sizing: smaller batches when KV miss ratio > X%.
- If we can cheaply detect multi-session interleaving pattern, prefer session-local KV pinning for the active thread pool.
